proposed_ledger_entry: Item 345 analyzes every ordinary Galois descent of Item 342's chosen-prime Kummer lift T in K_p=Q(zeta_(p-1)). Because p splits completely, the chosen Teichmueller prime has trivial decomposition group. The selected gate T in P kills only one split coordinate. Consequently no nontrivial trace, bounded-character projection, or additive Galois idempotent is forced to vanish at the prime below P. Relative norms do preserve the gate, but for H of size h the relative norm has conjugate bound (21 sqrt(p))^h in a field of degree phi(p-1)/h, so its absolute norm bound is exactly (21 sqrt(p))^phi(p-1), independent of the intermediate field. Thus bounded-index and bounded-degree subfields do not improve the black-box height. A genuine degree-D descent would require a stabilizer of size at least phi(p-1)/D, which is not forced by chosen-prime membership. Five preselected exact group-ring controls all have trivial stabilizer; the two selected-zero controls retain full cyclotomic orbit, while two nonzero controls have p-divisible norms because another split coordinate vanishes, proving exact norm false positives. No scan or universal claim is used. The only live descent routes require a new large-stabilizer theorem on selected-zero rows, exceptional norm cancellation, an extra full-collision condition, or chosen-prime p-adic nonconcentration. Booking and ceiling reduction remain zero; the fixed-j1 ceiling remains 1/36 per 6M.
